name: Custody transfer metering
principle: Custody transfer metering measures commercial quantities of oil, gas and products to contractual accuracy with auditable traceability. Gas stations use ultrasonic or orifice meters with pressure, temperature and composition (gas chromatograph) inputs computing flow to agreed standards (AGA reports, ISO 17089); liquid meters (turbine, coriolis, PD) are proved against prover loops or master meters. Fiscal-class systems add sampling, calibration records, uncertainty budgets and redundant computation under OIML or national type approval.

process_steps.name: Primary meter measures flow with P, T and composition inputs
Flow computer computes standard volume or energy to the contract standard
Liquid meters proved against prover or master meter
Records, sampling and calibration evidence retained for audit

limitations: uncertainty budget is contractual: installation effects, calibration drift and composition errors all count
metering disputes cost more than the metering; documentation discipline is part of the system
advantages: energy-flow gas metering settles purchases on heat content, not just volume
proved liquid meters deliver fiscal accuracy over years with routine proving
